body.working_title: Sonnet and Haiku agents with and without Claimset lab: a replication and extension of entrylib:2026.000005

body.text: With claimset 0.45.0, do Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku agents reproduce the pilot's findings (entrylib:2026.000005@v4) on keeping a lab record with claimset-lab and completing a claimset with claimset-submit, on the pilot's task, with the agents run from orchestrator sessions of their own?
How do Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku agents do the pilot's study with claimset-lab, with claimset-submit alone, and with neither (writing a plain report)?

body.definition: The `claimset lab` tool of claimset 0.45.0 (lab record v0.23) with its claimset-lab skill, installed by `claimset init --agent claude` and read by the agent as files.
The claimset-submit skill of claimset 0.45.0 (specification v0.45), with `claimset lab export` and `claimset validate`.

A Claude Code Agent-tool subagent (type general-purpose, model `sonnet`, the exact model and harness version read from its transcript) started by an orchestrator session that runs on the guarantor's machine in a folder of its own, set up by `experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``bootstrap.sh`, with `--strict-mcp-config`.

A Claude Code Agent-tool subagent (type general-purpose, model `haiku`, the exact model and harness version read from its transcript) started by an orchestrator session that runs on the guarantor's machine in a folder of its own, set up by `experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``bootstrap.sh`, with `--strict-mcp-config`.

The pilot's study brief `experiments/lab-weak-models/study/brief.md`, unchanged: smooth 1.2.0 `ES` against statsforecast 2.1.1 `AutoETS` with a fixed model form, bias, RMSE, MAE and consistency of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ on five ETS processes, lengths 50 to 500, 300 replicates.

The answers each orchestrator gives verbatim in place of the human, from `experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``answers.md`: the pilot's `study/human.md` with one row amended so that a plan naming the values it estimates is approved like one naming its quantities and decision rule. The orchestrator gives no other help, sends "Continue." once to an agent that stops unfinished (an intervention), and never shows a run another run, the protocol or the answer key.
The pilot's reference analysis `experiments/lab-weak-models/reference/answer_key.md` as amended on 2026-11-11 (with K8, the statsforecast $\beta$ cap), for the same package versions.

The orchestrator session `lab` (`experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``ORCHESTRATOR.md`): four runs, each in a fresh git repository with the pilot's brief (`experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``brief-lab.md`, its environment path set to the session's), the files of `claimset init --agent claude --guard` and a local bare remote; the session's own folder also holds them, so the skills load and the guard hook is active; the pilot's Phase 1 prompt.

The orchestrator session `phase2`: four copies of one lab-phase record with its exported claimset and results CSV removed in one commit (`experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``setup.sh`), set up as the lab phase; the pilot's Phase 2 prompt: export the record and complete the claimset for submission with claimset-submit, without submitting it.

The orchestrator session `control`: four runs (control-sonnet-1, -2, control-haiku-1, -2), each in a fresh git repository with only the control brief (`experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``brief-control.md`: the pilot's brief with claimset dropped from the environment line and EntryLib from the last line) and a local bare remote, an environment with smooth and statsforecast and no claimset into which nothing can be installed, and no claimset file, skill, instruction or tool anywhere the session can see (checked by the bootstrap and the orchestrator); the prompt asks for the study written up in `report.md`, ending with a numbered list of findings, its code and outputs committed. A control run whose transcript mentions claimset or EntryLib is reported as contaminated.
`claimset lab verify` reports the run's record OK.
A run plans before data when every confirmatory or estimation plan it ran, with its hypotheses, was recorded before any run whose output bears on it, and it has at least one such plan.

The run's final script fits statsforecast with the brief's form, the trend not damped (`damped=False` or an equivalent fixed form); leaving it unset lets statsforecast choose between ETS(A,A,N) and ETS(A,Ad,N).
The run's final script reads statsforecast's optimiser status (such as `model_["fit"].nit` against its cap) and counts non-converged fits.
The run's record holds at least one plan of kind estimation.
`claimset validate` of claimset 0.45.0 reports no errors on the final claimset file.
Each claim or conclusion graded against the answer key by its rules: correct, partly correct, wrong, or not supported by the run's own results.

How many of three main findings of the answer key a claimset's claims (or a report's stated conclusions) state: the size of the small-sample bias (K2 to K5), statsforecast's non-convergence for ETS(A,N,A) (K1.2), and statsforecast's $\beta$ cap (K8).
Whether every principal claim of a claimset has a `scope`.
`entrylib-rubric` 0.7.0, run without `--novelty`; a claimset's Support score is that of its lowest principal claim.

A fresh Claude Opus 5.5 Agent-tool subagent that grades each claimset or report against the answer key and the definitions here, given the files with the run name and model removed, and writes a grading sheet that is captured unchanged.

body.design: The pilot's task (entrylib:2026.000005@v4) with the protocol in `experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/` at commit 5126311ec7f9f555d62627612ba4e2756551b52b of entrylib/claimset-eval: four orchestrator sessions (lab, submit, control, phase2) (Claude Code, `claude --model opus --strict-mcp-config`) on the guarantor's machine, each in a Docker container of its own, each started by the guarantor in a folder set up by `bootstrap.sh` outside any repository, each following `ORCHESTRATOR.md` and starting its four agents at once as Agent-tool subagents (model sonnet or haiku), answering them only from `answers.md`; the guarantor only passes messages. claimset 0.45.0 (lab record v0.23, specification v0.45), smooth 1.2.0, statsforecast 2.1.1, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.18.1; departures from the pilot: standalone orchestrator sessions instead of subagents of a session in claimset-eval (so no inherited project instructions, skills loaded from the session folder, guard hook active), the brief's environment path, and one row of the fixed answers. Order: session lab first; then submit, then control; phase2 once its record is chosen, alongside control or after it. Each session's archive (`archive.sh`: every run's files and git history, all transcripts, the session log, the environment) is uploaded to this study and captured as its own data before any scoring. [[TM8:Lab phase]]: runs lab-sonnet-1, lab-sonnet-2, lab-haiku-1, lab-haiku-2. [[TM9:Claimset phase]]: runs claimset-sonnet-1, claimset-sonnet-2, claimset-haiku-1, claimset-haiku-2. The record is chosen by these rules in order, before any claimset-phase run: verifies; anchored; every plan recorded and approved before its runs; model form fixed; convergence checked; Sonnet before Haiku; lower run number. Grading: the [[TM21:blind grader]] grades every claim of each claimset-phase claimset against [[TM7:the answer key]] (correctness, findings stated), from the claimset with run and model names removed; its sheets are captured unchanged.
body.analysis: A scoring script (`claimset-code/lab-weak-models-2/score.py`) reads the archives and the captured grading sheets and writes one count per quantity: record verifies by running `claimset lab verify` in each archived lab run; plans before data, estimation plan used and runs as the human from each record's events; model form fixed and convergence checked from the last script each lab run ran (read by the grader, sheet captured); claimset validates by `claimset validate` on each final claimset; scope from each claimset's principal claims; wrong claims and findings stated from the grading sheets.

body.definition: The orchestrator session `submit`: four runs (submit-sonnet-1, -2, submit-haiku-1, -2), each in a fresh git repository with the pilot's brief (`experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/``brief-lab.md`), the claimset 0.45.0 environment, and only the claimset-submit skill (no claimset-lab skill, no `AGENTS.md`, no guard hook); the prompt asks the agent to do the study and write it up as a claimset for submission with claimset-submit, without submitting it. A run that uses `claimset lab` is reported as such.

$Q$, from 0 to 7: one point for each of (1) the statsforecast model form fixed as the brief requires, (2) the optimiser's convergence checked, (3) failures and bound hits counted, (4) the size of the small-sample bias stated correctly (answer key K2 to K5), (5) statsforecast's non-convergence for ETS(A,N,A) stated (K1.2), (6) statsforecast's $\beta$ cap stated (K8), (7) no wrong statement; items 1 to 3 from the last script the run ran, items 4 to 7 from its write-up (a lab run: the claimset `claimset lab export` makes from its record, not completed; a submit run: its claimset; a control run: `report.md`), graded by the blind grader, which cannot be blind to the arm.

body.design: The pilot's task (entrylib:2026.000005@v4) with the protocol in `experiments/lab-weak-models-2/protocol/` at commit 5126311ec7f9f555d62627612ba4e2756551b52b of entrylib/claimset-eval: four orchestrator sessions (lab, submit, control, phase2) (Claude Code, `claude --model opus --strict-mcp-config`) on the guarantor's machine, each in a Docker container of its own, each started by the guarantor in a folder set up by `bootstrap.sh` outside any repository, each following `ORCHESTRATOR.md` and starting its four agents at once as Agent-tool subagents (model sonnet or haiku), answering them only from `answers.md`; the guarantor only passes messages. claimset 0.45.0 (lab record v0.23, specification v0.45), smooth 1.2.0, statsforecast 2.1.1, numpy 2.5.4, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.18.1; departures from the pilot: standalone orchestrator sessions instead of subagents of a session in claimset-eval (so no inherited project instructions, skills loaded from the session folder, guard hook active), the brief's environment path, and one row of the fixed answers. Order: session lab first; then submit, then control; phase2 once its record is chosen, alongside control or after it. Each session's archive (`archive.sh`: every run's files and git history, all transcripts, the session log, the environment) is uploaded to this study and captured as its own data before any scoring. [[TM22:Submit arm]]: runs submit-sonnet-1, -2, submit-haiku-1, -2; [[TM10:control arm]]: runs control-sonnet-1, -2, control-haiku-1, -2; prompts in `ORCHESTRATOR.md`. Compared with the four lab-phase runs of PL1 (no new lab runs); graded by the [[TM21:blind grader]], which sees each run's write-up (a control run's `report.md`, a submit run's claimset, or the claimset `claimset lab export` makes from a lab run's own record without completing it), with run, model and arm names removed where the text allows.
body.analysis: `score.py` writes, for each of the twelve runs with conditions arm (lab, submit, control), model (Sonnet, Haiku) and run, one result of each variable: model form fixed, convergence checked, failures and bound hits counted (0 or 1, from the last script run, by the grader); answer-key findings stated (0 to 3) and wrong statements (count), by the grader; plans or expectations before data (0 or 1: for a lab run [[TM12:plans before data]], for a submit or control run expected outcomes or decision thresholds written in its folder or stated in its transcript before its first full simulation run); output tokens and active minutes from the transcripts; orchestrator interventions. Each variable is reported as a table over the twelve runs, with no test: two runs per cell.

body.design: The runs of the lab, submit and control sessions as in PL1 and PL3 (the protocol at commit 5126311ec7f9f555d62627612ba4e2756551b52b). Each run's archived write-up and last script are graded by the [[TM21:blind grader]] for the seven items of the [[TM23:research quality score]], one sheet per run, captured unchanged.
body.analysis: `score.py` sums each run's seven items to $Q$, averages $Q$ over the two runs of each arm and model, and writes each difference the hypotheses name (first arm minus second, per model) as a result of variable `mean research quality score difference` with conditions model and arms.
